title: Light, law, and learning prepare the elders to build Zion
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at a conference of high priests in Kirtland, Ohio, on 27–28 December 1832. The elders had prayed, one by one, to learn God’s will about building Zion. His scribe wrote it down, and the original manuscript is lost. On 11 January 1833 Joseph sent a copy to William W. Phelps in Missouri and called it an “olive leaf”. Verses 127–137 come from a separate revelation of 3 January 1833 on the school of the prophets, later printed with this one.
summary: The revelation tells the assembled elders their prayers were heard and promises “another Comforter”. It names the light of Christ as the power in the sun, moon, stars, and earth. That light gives life to all things and is the law that governs them. The earth will be sanctified for celestial beings, and each person receives the glory whose law he can abide. A parable of a lord visiting twelve servants, each in his hour, pictures God visiting his kingdoms. The elders must call a solemn assembly, sanctify themselves, teach one another, and seek learning “by study and also by faith”. Seven angels then sound trumpets over the Second Coming, the resurrections, and Michael’s final battle with the devil. The elders must build a house of God, and the closing verses set rules for the school of the prophets.

contextNote.title: Learning by study and by faith
contextNote.text: The elders had asked how to build Zion, and much of the answer was about learning. Verse 118 begins with a problem: “all have not faith”. Its remedy is to teach one another and to seek “out of the best books”. Verses 78–79 show how wide the subjects are, from doctrine to history, nations, and countries. Verse 80 gives the reason: the elders are being prepared to be sent out again. Verse 119 then gives the learning a place, a house that is also “a house of learning”. In this passage, seeking learning is preparation for a mission, pursued through both study and faith.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for section 88, “Establish … a House of God,” ties the command to build a house to holiness and learning. According to verses 119–125, what kind of people did the Lord want gathering in that house?
reviewNote: Read all 141 verses. Official heading gives Kirtland, 27–28 December 1832 and 3 January 1833, a conference of high priests praying about the upbuilding of Zion, and Joseph Smith’s “olive leaf” description. JSP introduction read for Williams as scribe, the lost original, and the 11 January 1833 letter to Phelps. A second JSP document, “Revelation, 3 January 1833 [D&C 88:127–137]” (https://www.josephsmithpapers.org/paperSummary/revelation-3-january-1833-dc-88127-137), was also read; it covers verses 127–137 only, so the origin of verses 138–141 (washing of feet) is not settled here. Michael (v. 112) is not added as a person; Latter-day Saint teaching identifies him with Adam, but the text names only Michael. Month set to the first date. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes
